headline: The 8 PM HRRR brought back a Friday-morning shower burst (0.33 in in 3 hours, about 5 to 8 AM) right as the 7.9 ft high tide comes in with ~1.8 ft of surge, but the other models stay light and the consensus is only 0.18 in: no street flooding expected, worth a look at dawn.

summary.text: HRRR's 8 PM run brought back a Friday-morning burst: 0.02 in up to 0.33 in in its wettest 3 hours (about 5 to 8 AM). Consensus edged up from 0.12 to 0.18 in.
Wettest 3 hours, next 72 h: HRRR 0.33 in, GFS 0.33 (copies HRRR), RRFS 0.18, NBM 0.12, ECMWF 0.08. Consensus (HRRR ×1.25 = 0.41, RRFS 0.18, NBM 0.12: middle value) 0.18 in.
Most likely nothing beyond the gutters. If HRRR's burst verifies, water may briefly reach the sidewalk. Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour.
Scattered showers overnight, a first HRRR pulse about 2 to 4 AM, the main one about 6 to 8 AM Friday, then drying by midday. Light showers again Saturday afternoon or evening.
The burst lines up with the rising tide: 7.9 ft high at 8:32 AM runs ~9.7 ft on NOAA's Bay model. Channel low: Caltrain 0.07 ft (5:13 PM), Monitoring 2.8 ft.
No need to move cars tonight. Check the page between 5 and 9 AM Friday; if the 1-hour alarm trips, move cars out of the cul-de-sac and watch the drains.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: The surface low that brought Thursday's thunderstorms has moved inland. NWS San Francisco's 9:42 PM aviation update expects scattered showers to continue through the night and drop off around midday Friday, with an isolated thunderstorm possible about 5 to 8 AM Friday (less than 10% chance) that could bring heavy rain, small hail and gusty winds. Friday afternoon turns partly sunny and cold. A weak front late Saturday is expected to fizzle as it moves south, leaving post-frontal showers into Monday morning. The next system to watch arrives Tuesday into Wednesday (NWS mentions 1 to 3 in for the North Bay and coastal ranges), together with the king tides of November 24 to 26.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since the 4:20 PM discussion, the HRRR has flip-flopped again. The 8 PM run brings back a shower band early Friday: 0.07 and 0.10 in in the hours ending 3 and 4 AM, then 0.16 and 0.17 in in the hours ending 7 and 8 AM. Its wettest 3 hours are now 0.33 in (about 5 to 8 AM), up from 0.02 in, with a storm total of 0.65 in through Saturday afternoon. Its 15-minute output puts the heaviest rain about 6:45 to 8 AM (0.23 in in its wettest 3 hours), no single 15 minutes above 0.07 in. GFS shows exactly the same numbers for Friday morning, so it is repeating the HRRR rather than confirming it.

The independent models are lighter but agree on the timing: NBM is unchanged at 0.12 in, wettest about 2 to 5 AM with its biggest hour (0.06 in) ending 7 AM. The new RRFS run (10 AM, replacing the 4 AM run) dropped from 0.39 to 0.18 in; it has 0.06 and 0.08 in in the hours ending 6 and 7 AM Friday, but its wettest 3 hours are a light round Saturday evening around 8 to 11 PM. ECMWF eased from 0.15 to 0.08 in, a steady drizzle-like 0.02 to 0.03 in per hour from 1 to 10 AM Friday.

The dashboard's consensus (HRRR ×1.25 = 0.41, RRFS 0.18, NBM 0.12; middle value) is 0.18 in, up from 0.12 in. Because every model now favors early Friday morning and the HRRR has a history of under-forecasting local bursts, I think the consensus is a fair middle but the HRRR deserves a look: its biggest hour, 0.17 in, would have to triple to reach the 0.40 in burst alarm. HRRR's lone 0.16 in hour Saturday around 3 to 4 PM has no support from the other models and is a low-confidence shower cell.

Storm totals for the next 72 hours: HRRR 0.65 in (its run ends Saturday 4 PM), GFS 0.60, ECMWF 0.43, RRFS 0.41, NBM 0.37.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
The Bay is still running about 1.8 ft above the predicted tide on NOAA's Bay model. Tonight's 6.2 ft high at 8:09 PM showed about 8.0 ft. After the 2:07 AM low (1.6 ft predicted, about 3.2 ft on the model) the water rises quickly through the Friday-morning showers: about 7.1 ft at 6 AM, 8.5 ft at 7 AM and 9.5 ft at 8 AM, peaking near 9.7 ft with the 7.9 ft high at 8:32 AM. That is the worst overlap of the event, since high Bay water slows how fast the channel drains, though with rates this light it should not matter much. Saturday's 8.4 ft high at 9:06 AM runs about 10.1 ft on the model; Sunday's 8.8 ft at 9:42 AM is beyond the model run.

The Coastal Flood Advisory for the Bay shoreline continues until 11 AM Saturday, with up to 1.8 ft of surge, and NWS expects to upgrade the Bays to a Coastal Flood Warning as the king tides approach.

Channel: the gauge upstream of Caltrain last reported 0.07 ft at 5:13 PM (no newer reading in the county feed), far below Flood Monitoring (2.8 ft). At Alameda de las Pulgas it is 0.26 ft at 10 PM, steady (Monitoring 3.18 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Mostly a lull. The Caltrain rain gauge recorded 0.04 in in the 7 PM hour (last tip 7:01 PM) and nothing since: 0.04 in over the last 6 hours and 0.44 in over 24 hours. The channel is low and steady.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Moderate on timing, low on impact. Every model now points at early Friday morning, but only the HRRR (and GFS, which copies it) puts a real burst in it, and the HRRR has put a cell in a different place in each of its last several runs. Even its 0.33 in is well under the Yellow line. The realistic wildcard is a short thunderstorm (NWS gives it under 10%) dumping a heavy half hour on wet ground right as the high tide peaks. Most likely outcome: wet streets, full gutters, no flooding.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• No need to move cars out of the cul-de-sac tonight.
• Glance at the dashboard between 5 and 9 AM Friday. If the 1-hour burst alarm trips (0.40 in in one hour), move cars and watch the street drain grates.
• Clear leaves from the street drain grates and yard drains when it's light; more rain is likely Tuesday and Wednesday with the king tides.
• If water does reach the sidewalk, a timestamped photo at the peak helps tune the dashboard.
• Cold morning Friday and Saturday. Don't drive or walk through moving water.
